patient_assessment_using_mini_mental_sta.assessment: The MMSE score is not directly presented; chart describes severe cognitive impairment, but no quantitative value.

__THRESH__::patient_assessment_using_min.assessment: No explicit MMSE score or range is given; defer threshold assessment to visit.
No explicit MMSE score or range is given; defer threshold assessment to visit.

patient_is_capable_of_self_locomotion_no.assessment: Chart states: 'He is unable to...walk independently,' thus patient cannot walk without assistance.

patient_is_capable_of_locomotion_with_as.assessment: Chart describes unable to walk independently, but does not mention walking with an assistive device; defer to visit.

patient_has_diagnosis_of_alzheimer_s_dis.assessment: Six months of progressive memory loss, aphasia, abnormal behavior, and functional loss in an elderly patient fits clinical Alzheimer's, but the diagnosis is not explicitly stated; defer to visit.

patient_has_finding_of_has_a_carer_now.assessment: Patient brought in by wife and son who are involved in care, implying presence of carer.
patient_has_finding_of_has_a_carer_now.evidence: An 89-year-old man was brought to the emergency department by his wife and son.

patient_has_symptoms_of_delusions_now.assessment: Chart describes notable abnormal behaviors and personality changes, but no explicit presence of delusions.

patient_has_symptoms_of_delusions_now@@p.assessment: Chart is silent on delusions, both in symptom type and duration.

patient_has_symptoms_of_hallucinations_n.assessment: The chart describes cognitive deficits, personality changes, and unusual behaviors (e.g., reaching for objects that are not real), but it does not explicitly state hallucinations (visual, auditory, etc.), nor is there strong clinical inference for hallucinations specifically.
There is no explicit or inferred documentation of hallucinations occurring for one month or longer; the chart is silent on this specific duration qualifier.

patient_has_finding_of_has_a_proxy_now.assessment: The patient is brought by wife and son, who are acting in a caregiving or proxy capacity.
patient_has_finding_of_has_a_proxy_now.evidence: "An 89-year-old man was brought to the emergency department by his wife and son..."

patient_is_non_institutionalized_now.assessment: There is no mention of the patient being institutionalized; he is brought from home to the emergency department, suggesting he is not institutionalized.
patient_is_non_institutionalized_now.evidence: "An 89-year-old man was brought to the emergency department by his wife and son" (no indication he lives in an institution)

patient_has_diagnosis_of_amnestic_disord.assessment: The patient has profound recent memory impairment, being unable to recall words after 5 minutes and having family-reported poor memory; this supports a current amnestic disorder as part of his dementia.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_amnestic_disord.evidence: He could immediately recall three out of three words but recalled none of them after 5 minutes. ... He began to have poor memory, difficulty expressing himself...

patient_is_exposed_to_anti_psychotic_age.assessment: There is no mention of past or current use of antipsychotic medications in the chart.
patient_is_exposed_to_anti_psychotic_age.evidence: silent: no mention of antipsychotic exposure

patient_is_exposed_to_anti_psychotic_age.assessment: Since there is no evidence of any antipsychotic exposure, there cannot be exposure for an adequate period with a therapeutic dose.
patient_is_exposed_to_anti_psychotic_age.evidence: silent: no mention of antipsychotic exposure

patient_is_exposed_to_anti_psychotic_age.assessment: Since there is no evidence of any prior antipsychotic treatment, there cannot be evidence of refractoriness.
patient_is_exposed_to_anti_psychotic_age.evidence: silent: no mention of antipsychotic exposure or refractoriness

patient_is_exposed_to_anti_psychotic_age.assessment: There is no evidence of antipsychotic use, thus none used to treat psychotic symptoms.
patient_is_exposed_to_anti_psychotic_age.evidence: silent: no mention of antipsychotic use for psychotic symptoms

patient_has_diagnosis_of_bipolar_disorde.assessment: No evidence in the chart supports a current or past diagnosis of bipolar disorder.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_bipolar_disorde.evidence: silent: no mention of bipolar disorder

patient_has_diagnosis_of_delirium_now.assessment: The patient is alert, with a six-month progression of symptoms and no acute onset or fluctuating consciousness to suggest delirium.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_delirium_now.evidence: The patient was alert and oriented to self and city but not year... six months of progressive changes

patient_has_diagnosis_of_dementia_co_occ.assessment: There is no mention of HIV infection or HIV-related dementia in the chart.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_dementia_co_occ.evidence: silent: no mention of HIV infection or HIV-associated dementia

patient_has_finding_of_dementia_due_to_h.assessment: There is no history of head trauma or evidence that dementia is due to trauma.
patient_has_finding_of_dementia_due_to_h.evidence: silent: no mention of head trauma

patient_has_finding_of_dementia_due_to_p.assessment: No mention or evidence of Parkinson's disease or symptoms suggesting Parkinsonian dementia.
patient_has_finding_of_dementia_due_to_p.evidence: silent: no mention of Parkinson's disease

patient_has_finding_of_dementia_due_to_p.assessment: The chart does not mention Pick's disease specifically; while behavioral changes and speech/language disturbance could be compatible with frontotemporal or Pick's disease, there is no explicit diagnosis.
patient_has_finding_of_dementia_due_to_p.evidence: silent: no diagnosis of Pick's disease in the chart

patient_has_diagnosis_of_dementia_now.assessment: The patient has six months of progressive cognitive and functional decline, inability to perform activities of daily living, prominent memory loss, and is not oriented to year, all clearly consistent with current dementia.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_dementia_now.evidence: An 89-year-old man was brought... after six months of progressive changes in cognition and personality. He is unable to dress, bathe, use the toilet, or walk independently. He could not follow commands involving multiple steps...

patient_has_diagnosis_of_dementia_now@@c.assessment: There is no documentation of a reversible cause of the patient's dementia (e.g., thyroid disorder, B12 deficiency, normal-pressure hydrocephalus, etc.), nor any hint of acute delirium or metabolic disturbance.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_dementia_now@@c.evidence: silent: no evidence of reversible cause of dementia in the chart

patient_has_finding_of_dementia_now@@spe.assessment: While the behavioral and executive dysfunction could suggest a non-Alzheimer's dementia, there is no explicit diagnosis of a specific non-Alzheimer's dementia (e.g., frontal/temporal variant, Pick's, etc.).
patient_has_finding_of_dementia_now@@spe.evidence: silent: no diagnosis of specific non-Alzheimer's type dementia

patient_has_finding_of_dementia_now.assessment: This variable is a duplicate; assessment as above: chart gives clear evidence of dementia due to functional and cognitive losses.
patient_has_finding_of_dementia_now.evidence: see above: 'six months of progressive changes in cognition and personality... unable to dress, bathe, use the toilet, or walk independently... not oriented to year'

patient_has_finding_of_dementia_of_front.assessment: Although the patient has prominent behavioral symptoms, language changes and poor executive function which are compatible with frontal lobe dementia, there is no explicit diagnosis or strong enough clinical evidence to assert this specifically.
patient_has_finding_of_dementia_of_front.evidence: silent: no diagnosis of frontal lobe dementia

patient_has_finding_of_frontotemporal_de.assessment: Symptoms such as behavioral change, language disturbance, and executive dysfunction are present, which can be seen in frontotemporal dementia, but there is no chart text naming frontotemporal dementia or providing strong definitive evidence (such as imaging or professional diagnosis).
patient_has_finding_of_frontotemporal_de.evidence: silent: no diagnosis of frontotemporal dementia in chart

patient_has_finding_of_senile_dementia_o.assessment: There is no evidence or history of visual hallucinations, parkinsonism, or fluctuating cognition to suggest Lewy body dementia, and no explicit diagnosis in the chart.
patient_has_finding_of_senile_dementia_o.evidence: silent: no diagnosis of Lewy body dementia or supporting clinical features

patient_has_finding_of_major_depressive_.assessment: There is no mention in the chart of depressed mood, anhedonia, or other core features of major depressive episodes; the described presentation is of dementia with behavioral changes but no evident depressive syndrome.
patient_has_finding_of_major_depressive_.evidence: silent: no mood symptoms or depressive episode described; behavioral changes are not depressive per se

patient_has_finding_of_major_depressive_.assessment: There is no mention of a major depressive episode; therefore, no evidence of psychotic (delusional) features within one.
patient_has_finding_of_major_depressive_.evidence: silent: no major depressive episode or delusions described

patient_has_finding_of_major_depressive_.assessment: There is no mention of a major depressive episode or hallucinations; thus, no evidence for this criterion.
patient_has_finding_of_major_depressive_.evidence: silent: no major depressive episode or hallucinations described

patient_has_diagnosis_of_mood_disorder_w.assessment: The patient is not described as having a mood disorder (such as bipolar or major depressive disorder) nor any psychotic features in that context.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_mood_disorder_w.evidence: silent: all described symptoms are cognitive/behavioral, not mood or psychosis

patient_has_finding_of_multi_infarct_dem.assessment: There is no mention of a history of strokes, stepwise decline, or imaging evidence of infarcts; the clinical picture is of a progressive dementia, not multi-infarct dementia.
patient_has_finding_of_multi_infarct_dem.evidence: silent: no cerebrovascular history, no multi-infarct dementia described

patient_has_diagnosis_of_psychoactive_su.assessment: The chart contains no mention of current or past substance use or substance use disorder.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_psychoactive_su.evidence: silent: no substance use history noted

patient_has_diagnosis_of_psychoactive_su.assessment: There is no mention of any (significant or otherwise) psychoactive substance use disorder in the history.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_psychoactive_su.evidence: silent: no significant substance use disorder referenced

patient_has_diagnosis_of_psychoactive_su.assessment: There is no mention of any psychoactive substance use disorder in the patient’s history.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_psychoactive_su.evidence: silent: no substance use disorder referenced

patient_has_diagnosis_of_psychoactive_su.assessment: The patient’s history contains no mention of substance use disorder within the past 6 months.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_psychoactive_su.evidence: silent: no substance use disorder within 6 months referenced

patient_has_finding_of_psychotic_symptom.assessment: The patient is described as exhibiting unusual behaviors (pouring milk onto the table, undressing, grabbing at examiner) but there is no mention of delusions or hallucinations, which are the psychotic symptoms specified by the trial.
There is no explicit mention or strong clinical suggestion that any current psychotic symptoms (if present) would be better explained by another general medical condition.
patient_has_finding_of_psychotic_symptom.evidence: silent: no alternate medical condition specified as cause

patient_has_finding_of_psychotic_symptom.assessment: There is no mention of substance use or exposure contributing to symptoms.
There is no claim that any psychotic symptoms (if present) predated the onset of dementia; behavioral changes are described as new during the last 6 months.
patient_has_finding_of_psychotic_symptom.evidence: silent: onset of symptoms in last 6 months

patient_has_diagnosis_of_schizoaffective.assessment: There is no mention of schizoaffective disorder in the chart.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_schizoaffective.evidence: silent: no mention of schizoaffective disorder

patient_has_diagnosis_of_schizophrenia_n.assessment: There is no mention of schizophrenia in the chart.

patient_has_diagnosis_of_seizure_disorde.assessment: The patient has myoclonic jerks (on exam), but there is no mention of a seizure disorder diagnosis.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_seizure_disorde.evidence: silent: myoclonus noted, but no seizure disorder diagnosis

patient_has_finding_of_substance_induced.assessment: There is no evidence in the chart for a history of substance-induced persistent dementia.
patient_has_finding_of_substance_induced.evidence: silent: no mention of substance use or substance-induced dementia

patient_has_finding_of_dementia_of_tempo.assessment: There is no diagnosis in the chart of temporal lobe dementia or frontotemporal dementia.
patient_has_finding_of_dementia_of_tempo.evidence: silent: no mention of temporal lobe or frontotemporal dementia

patient_has_finding_of_traumatic_encepha.assessment: There is no mention of traumatic brain injury or chronic traumatic encephalopathy.
patient_has_finding_of_traumatic_encepha.evidence: silent: no mention of traumatic encephalopathy

patient_has_finding_of_vascular_dementia.assessment: The chart provides a description of progressive cognitive and behavioral decline consistent with dementia, but nowhere attributes this to vascular dementia or describes a history of strokes/TIAs, stepwise progression, or imaging findings supporting vascular etiology; chart is silent on a vascular cause.
patient_has_finding_of_vascular_dementia.evidence: silent: defer to exclusion default (no mention of vascular dementia, stroke, TIA, or supporting imaging findings)
